translations.text: His instruction.
i.e. this is peculiar to his pupil, because he was harsh.

i.e. I pray in many ways, as I asked, i.e. I pray God for you as earnestly as I besought you to stay in Ephesus, though that was earnest. Alternatively, he goes on to where he says, 'This instruction I commend to you, son Timothy', and what lies between them is a parenthesis.
i.e. it is for this that he declares [?] it.
i.e. genealogies and tales of origins.
i.e. no end is put to them.
in which each man attacks [?] the other.
i.e. they do not help the building up of faith.
i.e. that is better than anything.
i.e. that is the place where it dwells.
i.e. from the three things he mentioned before.
i.e. so that they might be making law with kings.
i.e. what they say does not fit.
i.e. the law was not given to punish the righteous, but to correct the guilty.
one who slays his kin.
i.e. to the [?].
to perjurers.
i.e. so that I might preach his glory.
i.e. I was insulting him.
i.e. so that I was healed of sin.
i.e. this is a statement of confirmation, or it is the heading of what follows.
i.e. it is plain from the fact that I was healed.
i.e. so that it might be an example of the healing of everyone.
i.e. patience with my sin, and my healing afterwards.
to the King of the ages.
i.e. it is fitting to praise him.
i.e. an end without end, for it is endlessly that he bestows his good gifts.
as was preached to you at first.
'having faith', i.e. it is thus that your soldiering will be good.

i.e. they have parted from it, i.e. their names are mentioned so that no one may take an example from them. That Alexander was a craftsman, as he himself says: 'Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil.'
i.e. of penitence; or 'to blaspheme', i.e. that they may not be blasphemous against [?], for they do not [?].
i.e. that is universal love.
i.e. provided that there is quiet and tranquillity for kings, we too shall then have those two, and piety and chastity along with that.

Question: why are not all saved if he desires it, since 'the Lord has done all things whatsoever he willed'? Not difficult: because no one is compelled to serve; or it is a part for the whole, for there is no race or language in the world of which someone has not been saved; or those whom he desires to save are those whom he has saved, only, i.e. 'who wills all men to be saved', saved, as Augustine says. Augustine: As though it were said that no man can be saved except the one whom he himself has willed to be saved.
as he names 'of all', he desires the salvation of all.
i.e. both himself and men.
he gave himself on the cross.
i.e. for the salvation of everyone.
i.e. testimony was given of it at the time when the redemption through the cross was accomplished.
i.e. this is the mystery of that testimony which I preach.
i.e. without anger.
i.e. an adornment that is fitting for faith.
with braids.
i.e. what is proper, i.e. generosity and chastity.
i.e. let her not ask anything in church, but let her ask her husband at home.
i.e. except to her children.
i.e. let her not be in authority.
for the man is sufficient for speaking.
i.e. the man is older and more steadfast than the woman.
i.e. it is thus, then, that the bearing of children will be salvation for her.
which he says below
i.e. martyrdom before all; or: let him do the works of a bishop
i.e. these are the works of a bishop which he speaks of below
before receiving orders, after baptism
in receiving everyone
i.e. that he be learned in knowledge and wisdom
i.e. he does not drink wine until he is drunk
i.e. he has no quarrel with anyone
i.e. not covetous
i.e. his sons obedient to him
i.e. if he has not corrected his household while he is without orders, the leadership of a multitude is not fitting for him
i.e. not a newcomer [?]
i.e. the punishment that came upon the devil after transgression, lest it come upon him
i.e. let everyone bear witness of him that orders are fitting for him
i.e. from the laity among whom he has been: what his conduct is, so that he may manage his household well before orders are conferred on him; it is clearer to declare it afterwards [?]
i.e. that what they say and what they think be not different; or: that they be not [?]
i.e. that they do not sell divine gifts for worldly gain
i.e. for they are preceptors of the faith
i.e. testimony is given about them before orders are conferred on them
i.e. for there were deaconesses there at that time
i.e. that is, before receiving orders
i.e. if they fulfil their order; or: among the laity, if they have corrected their household
i.e. a reward in the heavenly kingdom; or: it is fitting to confer the order of bishop on them
i.e. that you may remember my [?]; soon I shall come to you
i.e. I do not know my journeys [?]
i.e. teach it, and so that you may put it into practice.
i.e. it was then that the angels learned it, since he was in sovereignty over them themselves; or, he was made manifest to us by angels on the night of the birth.
i.e. through faith.
i.e. though this which has come to pass is wonderful, there will be a time when it will not be believed and will be denied.
i.e. this is what separates them from it.
i.e. what they teach and what they do are different [?].
i.e. cauterized, or burned.
i.e. so that thanksgiving might be given to God through them by the faithful.
i.e. if it is received with perfection of faith and with thanksgiving.
i.e. the meal is taken with praise.
i.e. if you teach these words.
i.e. which you have heard from me.
i.e. old tales of the Law which false apostles relate.
i.e. avoid.
i.e. the beauty of the body will not last long.
i.e. it is good here and there.
i.e. which he says below.
i.e. it is worthy of so much.
i.e. this is what is given [?] to us.
i.e. those are the king's special beloved ones.
i.e. so that everyone may take an example from you.
i.e. so that you may understand what you have read, i.e. in fulfilling it and in preaching it.
i.e. strengthening many in the faith.
i.e. when orders were conferred on you.
i.e. in fulfilling it.
i.e. so that everyone may know your perfection, so that everyone may take an example from you.
i.e. to fulfil it.
i.e. so that you may teach them.
i.e. its fulfilment and its teaching.
It will be salvation for you yourself.
i.e. everyone who has heard you teaching.
i.e. as if it were.
i.e. the old women.
i.e. as they have fostered her, let her care for them.
i.e. who are perfect.
i.e. of her own household.
i.e. if a widow has anyone, sons or parents, it is a reproach to the sons and the parents that she should be without care from them.
i.e. that believer is worse than the unbeliever.
i.e. this is the widow whom it is fitting for the church to maintain, on account of age and morals.
i.e. when she was among the laity.
i.e. these are the morals for which the church takes her.
i.e. when she was among the laity.
if she has received guests.
if she has shown humility.
i.e. if she has ministered to the people of the prison; she ministered, i.e. with food and clothing.
i.e. if nothing good was lacking from her deeds when she was among the laity, it is fitting to receive her into the church.
i.e. lest she go [?].
i.e. if they become wanton [?].
i.e. these are the morals of the widows who are quick [?] in faith.
i.e. going visiting, and being without doing anything.
i.e. womenfolk.
i.e. I prefer that to their being received into the church.
i.e. so that there may be no reproach of the divine grace through their sin; or 'maledicti gratia' [for the sake of reproach].
i.e. they have gone back again to the desires of the world.
i.e. that they may provide them with their livelihood.
i.e. so that their maintenance may not be needed in the church.
i.e. fulfilment of what they teach, and food and clothing for them.
i.e. those who preach and teach the word of God.
i.e. this is an example from the Old Law, to strengthen the point that it is right to maintain [?] and to clothe the people of holy orders and of learning.
i.e. it is right for everyone to have the reward of his labour.
i.e. to fix sin or an accusation upon him.
i.e. unless the two laws, the old and the new, fix sin upon him; or the three laws, i.e. of nature, etc. Only then is he liable to accusation, if it is not fulfilled by him.
i.e. let as many as know his sin know of his rebuke.
i.e. as many as hear of it.
i.e. I beseech, or 'adiuro' [I adjure].
i.e. 'cogitatione' [in thought] or 'consilio' [in counsel]: do not confer holy orders on anyone without knowing him beforehand.
i.e. to the south or to the north, unless it is done through good counsel.
i.e. do not confer holy orders on anyone until you know whether he is worthy of that order.
i.e. for if the one on whom he confers holy orders is sinful, his sins cling to the one who confers the order.
i.e. so that it may not be an increase of sickness for you.
i.e. make use of it.
for the sickness of the church is upon you.
for you are always sickly.

i.e. do not confer holy orders on anyone on account of his sin or of his good deeds; for there are some whose sins have been known before holy orders came upon them, and others whose sins have been known only afterwards; these, moreover, are brought to the Day of Judgement.
i.e. there are virtues in them, and they are manifest.
i.e. the other good deeds, it is long afterwards that they have become known.
i.e. it is hard to hide the good.
i.e. the instruction of the slaves here below.
i.e. so that it may not be said: 'Our slaves were obedient to us until the faith came, and they are disobedient now.'
i.e. I preach.
i.e. he is arrogant and he is ignorant.
i.e. he puts questions to everyone, and he does not like it if they are put to him.
i.e. contention of words.
i.e. of everyone against another.
i.e. about questions.
i.e. everyone passes judgement on another.
i.e. slanders and reproaches.
i.e. anyone who does that has no sense.
i.e. they say that it is for gain that God's will is to be done.
i.e. a sufficiency of food and clothing that will be enough, only.
i.e. we brought no provisions with us into this world.
i.e. we shall not carry any out of it, then.
i.e. a measure that may suffice us.
i.e. [?] it is she who has led them astray.
i.e. it is the laying of a hand on him [?], to be feeding greed.
i.e. that is the net with which the devil catches sinners.
i.e. there will always be desire.
i.e. to death.
i.e. they have parted from the faith.
i.e. they will have love [for it].
i.e. it is fitting for you
i.e. you have it in heaven
i.e. so that it may [?] on the day of death or of Judgement
as has been foretold to us
i.e. here is shown the worth of the person who will come: the more he is awaited [?]
i.e. it is [?] fitting for him
i.e. with the power of an apostle
i.e. it is he who is the source of the riches
i.e. so that their feasting in heaven may be good, and that they may be in the union of the body of Christ in heaven
i.e. thus is its equal measure
i.e. apart from sins, and a help to the world
i.e. the inquiry of the imperfect
i.e. from faith, or beyond faith
i.e. they have been kindled [?]
